/practicalAccordionItems/1/content/0.source_en: Non-slip winter footwear — the single most important item. All three stops have ice underfoot.

/practicalAccordionItems/1/content/1.source_en: Proper cold-weather layers: expect −5 °C or colder at Seoraksan with significant wind chill, and dusk temperatures at Eobi.

/practicalAccordionItems/1/content/2.source_en: Gloves, hat and something covering your ears. The Nami ferry deck is fully exposed.

/practicalAccordionItems/1/content/3.source_en: Small cash for Eobi's village-run fees and for lunch (₩10,000-15,000).

/practicalAccordionItems/1/content/4.source_en: Camera or smartphone, plus a spare battery — cold drains batteries fast, and this is a route people photograph heavily.

/practicalAccordionItems/1/preview.source_en: Non-slip winter footwear — the single most important item. All three stops…

/practicalAccordionItems/2/content/0.source_en: This is a winter-season tour and weather is part of the product, not an exception to it.

/practicalAccordionItems/2/content/1.source_en: The Eobi ice wall is not guaranteed. It is built by villagers over the coldest weeks and a warm spell shrinks or removes it. The village decides its own opening. If the wall is not viewable on your date we will tell you before departure and offer a rebooking or refund of that portion.

/practicalAccordionItems/2/content/2.source_en: The Seoraksan cable car is not guaranteed either. Its hours change daily and it suspends in strong wind or ice. It is not included in the price, so nothing is lost if it does not run.

/practicalAccordionItems/2/content/3.source_en: Heavy snow: the coach carries winter tyres and the tour normally still runs, but the return can take an extra hour. Severe snow or road closures can cancel the departure entirely — a full refund applies.

/practicalAccordionItems/2/content/4.source_en: The Nami ferry can be suspended in severe weather; if that happens the guide extends the other stops and the Nami admission is refunded.

/practicalAccordionItems/2/preview.source_en: This is a winter-season tour and weather is part of the product, not an exc…

/practicalAccordionItems/3/content/0.source_en: This is a winter-only itinerary. It exists because the Eobi Valley ice wall exists, and that is a seasonal, village-built structure rather than a permanent attraction.

/practicalAccordionItems/3/content/1.source_en: The wall typically begins forming from mid-December once the valley water freezes, and is most reliable through January and early February.

/practicalAccordionItems/3/content/2.source_en: Season end varies year to year — the 2025-26 season closed on 19 February. Dates for the coming winter are set by the village and confirmed at booking.

/practicalAccordionItems/3/content/3.source_en: Outside the season, the same Seoraksan and Nami Island pairing is available year-round on our Seoraksan + Nami Island + ⟦G0⟧ day tour.

/practicalAccordionItems/4/content/0.source_en: Two Seoul pickup points and the same two drop-off points, heated coach, licensed English-speaking guide.

/practicalAccordionItems/4/content/1.source_en: ⟦G0⟧ entrance — FREE since May 2023, no ticket needed.

/practicalAccordionItems/4/content/2.source_en: Nami Island round-trip ferry + Naminara Republic visa fee (₩19,000) — INCLUDED.

/practicalAccordionItems/4/content/4.source_en: NOT included: lunch and drinks (₩10,000-15,000, own expense), the Seoraksan cable car (₩16,000 adult round-trip, on-site tickets only and weather-dependent), Eobi Valley's on-site village fees (the ice-wall viewing area has been charged at about ₩1,000 per person, sled activities extra), Nami bicycle or e-buggy rental, and personal spending.

/practicalAccordionItems/4/content/5.source_en: Chinese-speaking guide available on request — please book at least 3 days ahead.

/practicalAccordionItems/4/preview.source_en: Two Seoul pickup points and the same two drop-off points, heated coach, lic…

/practicalAccordionItems/5/content/1.source_en: Chinese-speaking guide available on request — book 3+ days ahead.
/practicalAccordionItems/5/content/1.tm: Гид со знанием китайского доступен по запросу — бронируйте за 3 дня и более.

/practicalAccordionItems/5/content/2.source_en: Korean spoken throughout the day for menus, signage, and stall interactions; the guide handles translation.
/practicalAccordionItems/5/content/2.tm: В течение дня корейский звучит в меню, на указателях и при общении с продавцами; перевод берёт на себя гид.

/practicalAccordionItems/6/content/0.source_en: Moderate, and the difficulty here is ice rather than distance or gradient.

/practicalAccordionItems/6/content/1.source_en: Seoraksan: paved and stepped valley paths to Sinheungsa and the Tongildaebul, snowy and slippery in places. No hiking is scheduled and no summit is attempted.

/practicalAccordionItems/6/content/2.source_en: Nami Island: flat paved tree-lined avenues, ~3 km over two hours, icy underfoot in midwinter.

/practicalAccordionItems/6/content/3.source_en: Eobi Valley: a short, mostly flat wooden deck path to the viewing area — but the approach and surroundings are genuinely slippery. The ground beneath the ice wall is closed to visitors.

/practicalAccordionItems/6/content/4.source_en: Non-slip winter footwear is essential at all three stops. Ordinary trainers are not enough on this itinerary. Strollers and wheelchairs are not suitable at Eobi.

/practicalAccordionItems/6/preview.source_en: Moderate, and the difficulty here is ice rather than distance or gradient.

/practicalAccordionItems/7/content/0.source_en: Lunch is taken around 11:45 near Seoraksan or on the Sokcho side, straight after the park.

/practicalAccordionItems/7/content/1.source_en: East-coast choices: hoedeopbap (raw fish over rice), grilled fish, or Sokcho's well-known sundubu jjigae soft-tofu stew.

/practicalAccordionItems/7/content/2.source_en: Budget roughly ₩10,000-15,000 per person; cash and card are both normally accepted.

/practicalAccordionItems/7/content/3.source_en: The stop is a brisk 50 minutes — the two remaining stops are time-sensitive. Vegetarian options are limited, so tell the guide in the morning.
